title: Quarterly cadence lanes and commitment buffers for Hosted API + Model Catalog
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create a prescriptive playbook that maps quarterly cadence lanes (Commit, Hedge, Experiment) for the Hosted API and Model Catalog. The playbook must: 1) define decision windows for model onboarding/rotation and deprecation; 2) surface capacity commit buffer rules for Dedicated/Durable SKUs; 3) align OKRs across product, infra, and reliability; and 4) provide runbooks and gating criteria for canaries, rollback, and communication to customers. The deliverable is a single-page playbook + companion Confluence spec + rollout checklist for Q2 execution.
goals: Standardize quarterly decision windows so model onboarding and deprecation have predictable lead times
Reduce last-minute capacity churn by creating a buffer rule for reserved capacity that scales with model memory and request variability
Create explicit acceptance criteria and eval gates to prevent quality regressions during model rotation
Provide a single source of truth that maps product OKRs to release lanes and who owns each lane
acceptance_criteria: Playbook final draft reviewed and approved by Product, Infra, and Reliability leads
Confluence spec published with clear timelines, owners, and rollback criteria
Checklist and runbook created for canary windows, with at least one dry-run scheduled in Q2
Capacity buffer policy documented and validated against recent 90-day traffic variance (link to capacity dashboard included)
OKR mapping spreadsheet created and linked; owners assigned for each measurable
tasks: Draft initial playbook (owner: Marco) — PRD + 1-page executive summary
Gather inputs: 90-day traffic variability, top-10 model memory profiles (owner: Reliability)
Define commitment buffer formula (owner: Infra) — P50/P90 headroom rules
Draft gating criteria for model swap canary (owner: Applied ML) — perf and quality thresholds
Stakeholder review: Product, Eng, Reliability, Solutions — collect signoffs
Publish Confluence spec and link to Console dashboards + GitHub PR template
Schedule dry-run canary for one low-risk model in staging (owner: Eng)

Decision 2 (2026-02-28): Canary window minimum is 48 hours with a continuous monitoring hook to the Console (latency, errors, quality signals).
Decision 3 (2026-03-01): If Dedicated autoscaler toggle is unavailable, apply manual capacity hedges and escalate to Sales for any customer-facing throughput limits.

risks: Buffer formula may over-provision and increase cost if traffic volatility assumptions are wrong
If canary gating thresholds are too strict, model onboarding velocity will slow and backlog will grow
Manual enforcement for capacity hedges creates operational overhead and potential missed SLAs
Customer communication cadence not coordinated—risk of surprise deprecations causing churn

metrics: Lead time between model decision and production rollout (target: <= 30 days)
Number of unexpected deprecations or emergency rollbacks (target: 0 per quarter)
Hosted API cost delta due to buffer enforcement (target: < 6% increase net)
Canary false positive rate (sensitivity of gating thresholds; target: < 5%)
